newsitem.title: CHINA: China to repatriate Taiwan hijacker in mid-May.
newsitem.headline: China to repatriate Taiwan hijacker in mid-May.

text.p: China will repatriate in mid-May a Taiwanese who hijacked a domestic airliner from the island to the mainland in March, state radio said on Wednesday.
The Chinese Red Cross in the southeastern province of Fujian informed its Taiwan counterpart that Liu Shan-chung would be sent back to Taiwan on May 14 by sea.
"The Taiwan authorities concerned are requested to rapidly reply to the arrangement before May 7," the radio said.
Taiwan said earlier this month it had received a formal offer from China to send Liu back through the two sides' Red Cross organisations.
Liu commandeered a Taiwan commercial jet to Xiamen on March 10, becoming the first hijacker to force a passenger plane from the island to the mainland in the 1990s rather than the other direction.
China and Taiwan, enemies since a civil war split them in 1949, reached unofficial consensus on hijacker repatriation in 1995 but failed to sign the accord because of heightened political tensions.
